title: 12 Controls That Stop an AI Agent From Wiping Your Production Database
subtitle: For CTOs and ops leaders at 10-200 person SaaS companies. Tick 10 of 12 before any agent touches production, or you ship a future incident report with a deployment date.

sections.title: Credential & Permission Scoping
sections.description: An agent inherits whatever keys it can reach, so the keys are the real guardrail.

items.text: Issue a dedicated agent identity per environment, never a developer token, root key, or CI service account.
items.tip: One agent, one IAM role, one revocable key. If you can't kill it from a single console in under 30 seconds, it's wrong.

items.text: Scope every token to the narrowest resource and action set, read-only by default.
items.tip: The PocketOS agent found a blanket Railway CLI token sitting in the environment. Scoped to staging, the database would still exist.

items.text: Block destructive verbs at the IAM layer, not in the prompt.
items.tip: DELETE, DROP, TRUNCATE, rm -rf, volume:delete denied by policy. A system prompt that says 'never delete prod' is a request. An IAM deny is a wall.

items.text: Rotate agent credentials on a fixed cadence and on every model upgrade.

sections.title: Human-in-the-Loop Checkpoints
sections.description: The 15-20% of cases you route to a human is the design working, not the agent failing.

items.text: Require a named human to type the action for anything that mutates production state.
items.tip: 'Are you sure?' buttons get rubber-stamped. Forcing the operator to type the resource name forces them to actually read it.

items.text: Define the irreversibility threshold in writing and publish the list.
items.tip: Rule of thumb: anything a junior engineer can't undo in under 5 minutes needs human approval.

items.text: Route 15-20% of edge cases to a human queue by design.
items.tip: A 100% autonomous rate means your scope is too narrow or your guardrails are off. The review queue is the agent working correctly.

sections.title: Backup & Recovery Isolation
sections.description: If the agent can reach production, it must not be able to reach the backups.

items.text: Store backups on a separate volume, account, and credential scope from production.
items.tip: PocketOS lost the backups because they lived on the same Railway volume the agent deleted. Cross-account backups would have saved the company.

items.text: Test restore from backup monthly with a real recovery drill.
items.tip: Untested backups are theatre. You find out they're broken at the worst possible moment.

items.text: Maintain point-in-time recovery on the database itself, not just nightly snapshots.
items.tip: Supabase and most managed Postgres give you PITR. Turn it on before you need it.

sections.title: Action Logging & Anomaly Detection
sections.description: You can't investigate what you didn't record, and the agent can't be trusted to record itself.

items.text: Log every action with timestamp, tool call, arguments, and outcome to an append-only store the agent cannot write to.
items.tip: The PocketOS agent self-admitted what it did. That only helped because the logs survived. Put them somewhere the agent has no credentials for.

items.text: Alert on any first-time tool call, any call to a new resource, or any burst above 3x normal volume.
items.tip: An agent that has never touched the production volume suddenly issuing a delete against it is the alert. Catch the novelty, not just the failure.

sections.title: Scope & Blast Radius Controls
sections.description: Shrink what a single bad decision can reach before it reaches anything.

items.text: Constrain each agent to a single environment with its own credentials.
items.tip: One agent for staging, a separately credentialed agent for production. They share no keys, no env vars, no shell.

items.text: Wrap every tool the agent can call in a thin adapter that enforces scope, irreversibility checks, logging, and rate limits.
items.tip: The single most useful pattern here. The agent talks to your wrappers, never to raw SDKs or CLIs. It turns 'trust the model' into 'trust the wrapper.'
